kf: **Arterial ulcers** are caused by **peripheral arterial disease** and account for about 10–20% of leg ulcers (alone or mixed).
Punched-out, deep, painful ulcers on the toes, heel, lateral malleolus or shin; cold, hairless foot with weak pulses.
Pain worse on elevation and at night, eased by hanging the leg down.
Measure ABPI (toe pressures in diabetes); **never compress** an ischaemic limb.
Urgent vascular referral; same day for critical limb ischaemia. Stop smoking; antiplatelet and statin.

sub: Older smokers, people with diabetes, CKD, hypertension and hyperlipidaemia.

myths: **"All leg ulcers need compression"**: compression can cause gangrene in arterial disease.
patho_lead: Too little arterial blood reaches the skin, so it **dies from ischaemia**.

mech.t: Plaques narrow the arteries of the leg.
Distal skin receives too little oxygen, especially at pressure points and on elevation.
Minor trauma causes tissue death that cannot heal: a punched-out ulcer.
Rest pain, gangrene and tissue loss signal limb-threatening disease.

histo: Not used; diagnosis is clinical and vascular (ABPI, duplex, angiography).

sub: ABPI 0.5–0.8: reduced compression only under specialist guidance; below 0.5: no compression, urgent vascular.

comp: Infection, gangrene, amputation; high cardiovascular mortality.
